source_text:
Τί με τοῖς ἐμοῖς πολεμεῖς, τοῦ νόμου
προασπίζεις καὶ κατ' ἐμοῦ στρατεύεις, δι' ἐμὲ τρέχεις καὶ τοὺς ἐμοὺς κολάζεις; Τὴν
ἐμὴν δόξαν ἐκδικεῖς, ἀλλ' ἀγνοεῖς τὸ πόθεν ἅψασθαι χρὴ τῆς μάχης, πόθεν ἥκει
συγκροτῆσαι πόλεμον.»
5 Ταῦτα πρὸς τὸν Σαῦλον ὁ Χριστός· αὐτὸς δὲ ἀποκρίνεται καὶ λέγει· «Τίς εἶ,
κύριε;» Ἀγαθὸς ὁ τοῦ Παύλου ζῆλος, ἐπειδὴ κληθεὶς παραχρῆμα ὑπήκουσεν.
Ἐδέξατο τὸν λόγον καὶ παραχρῆμα τῆς ἀξίας τοῦ λαλοῦντος ᾔσθετο καὶ ἔλεγεν· «Τίς
εἶ, κύριε;» τῇ γὰρ αὐγῇ πεπλήρωμαι, ἑάλων τῷ φωτί, δεσμώ της τῆς ἀκτῖνος
γεγένημαι. «Τίς εἶ, κύριε;» Ποθῶ γάρ σου τὸ κάλλος ἰδεῖν, ἀναπτῆναι πρὸς τὰς
νεφέλας ἐπείγομαι, μαθεῖν ἐπι θυμῶ πόθεν τοῦτο τὸ «τῆς δόξης ἀπαύγασμα», τίς ὁ
τῆς τοσαύ της «χαρακτὴρ ὑποστάσεως», τίς οὗτος ὁ «φέρων τὰ πάντα τῷ ῥήματι τῆς
οἰκείας δυνάμεως». «Τίς εἶ, κύριε;» Ἤκουσα γάρ σου τῆς φωνῆς καὶ τοῦ νόμου
κεκόρεσμαι, οὐκέτι μοι τοῦ νόμου πόθος, οὐκέτι κιβωτὸν ἐθέλω χρυσόξυλον εἶναι,
ποθῶ φάτνην ἁγνὴν ἅπασαν βασιλικὴν χρυσόδωρον.» Πάντων τῶν αἱρετικῶν οἱ
παῖδες αἰσχυνέσθωσαν καὶ τὰ τῶν αἱρετικῶν ἐντρε πέσθωσαν στόματα. Ἰδοὺ γὰρ
κληθεὶς ὁ Παῦλος οὐ πολυπραγμο νεῖ ἀλλὰ μόνον πιστεύει, προσκυνεῖ καὶ οὐ
μάχεται, ὑμνολογεῖ καὶ ἡ μέμψις ἀπήλλακται. «Τίς εἶ, κύριε;» φησίν. Οὐκ ἂν δὲ
κύριον ἐκάλει, εἰ μὴ θεοῦ τοῦ καλοῦντος ᾐσθάνετο. Ὃν δὲ θεὸν ᾔδει ποιητὴν
ὡμολόγει, ὃν ὡμολόγει ποιητὴν ἀπαθῆ κατ ήγγελλεν, ἄφθαρτον εἶχεν. Ἔσεβεν ὡς
ἀθάνατον ἐκεῖνον οὗ τὸν σταυρὸν ᾔδει καὶ τὸν τάφον ἐγίνωσκεν. Οὐκ ἠγνόει τοὺς
κολάφους, τὴν λόγχην τῆς πλευρᾶς, τὰ ῥαπίσματα.
6 Τί δὲ ὅμως πρὸς αὐτὸν ὁ Χριστός; «Ἐγώ εἰμι Ἰησοῦς ὁ Ναζωραῖος ὃν σὺ
διώκεις.» Σύντομον τῆς πεύσεως τὴν ἀπό κρισιν λαμβάνει· «Ἐγώ εἰμι Ἰησοῦς ὁ
Ναζωραῖος ὃν σὺ διώκεις», ἐγώ εἰμι Ἰησοῦς ὁ ποτὲ καὶ νῦν, ὁ πρὸ πάντων καὶ μετὰ
πάντας, ὁ ἐν ἀρχῇ καὶ ἐπ' ἐσχάτων, ὁ τοῦ ∆αυὶδ υἱὸς ἀλλ' αὐτὸς πρὸ ∆αυίδ, ὁ ἐξ
Ἀβραὰμ ποιητής, ὁ ἐξ Ἀδὰμ ἀλλ' αὐτὸς τὸν Ἀδὰμἐκεράμευσεν, ἐξ Ἰσαὰκ ἀλλ' αὐτὸς
τοῦ Ἰσαὰκ τὸν βωμὸν ἐστε-φάνωσεν, ἐξ Ἰακὼβ ἀλλ' αὐτὸς ἐπὶ τῆς κλίμακος τοῖς
δήμοις τῶν ἀγγέλων κυκλούμενος ἐθεάσατο. «Ἐγώ εἰμι Ἰησοῦς ὃν σὺ διώκεις»,
ἀλλὰ διώκων οὐ φθάνεις· ποῦ γὰρ ἢ πῶς θηρά σεις «τὸ τῆς δόξης ἀπαύγασμα»;
thought_title: Christ questions Saul; Paul answers with faith
orientation: Christ continues his speech to Saul on the road, asking why Saul fights him with his own gifts; Saul answers 'Who are you, Lord?' and the homilist praises his immediate faith.
pass_a_gloss: Why [do] you make war [on] me with my own [things], [you] fight [on] behalf of the law and [you] march [in] battle against me, [you] run because of me and [you] punish my [people]? [You] avenge my glory, but [you] do not know from where [it] is necessary to lay hold of the battle, from where [it] comes to join together [the] war." These [things] to Saul the Christ [said]; but he answers and says: "Who are you, Lord?" Good [is] the zeal of Paul, since having been called immediately he obeyed. He received the word and immediately he perceived the worth of the [one] speaking and he said: "Who are you, Lord?" For with the brightness I have been filled, I have been captured by the light, a prisoner of the ray I have become. "Who are you, Lord?" For I long to see your beauty, to fly up to the clouds I hasten, to learn I desire from where this "radiance of glory" [is], who the [one] of such great "imprint of substance" [is], who this [one] "bearing all things by the word of his own power" [is]. "Who are you, Lord?" For I have heard your voice and of the law I have had my fill, no longer [is there] for me longing for the law, no longer [do] I wish [the] ark to be gold-wooded, I long [for] a pure manger entirely royal gold-gifted." Of all the heretics let the children be ashamed and of the heretics let the mouths be put to shame. For behold having been called Paul [does] not busy himself but only believes, worships and [does] not fight, sings hymns and the blame has been removed. "Who are you, Lord?" he says. But he would not have called [him] Lord, if he had not perceived God the [one] calling. And whom he knew [as] God he confessed [as] maker, whom he confessed [as] maker [as] impassible he proclaimed, incorruptible he held. He revered as immortal that [one] whose cross he knew and whose tomb he recognized. He was not ignorant of the blows, the spear of the side, the slaps.

lemmas.gloss: let them be put to shame
he busies himself with many questions

choices.english: I have had my fill of the Law
choices.why: Renders the perfect passive of κορέννυμι with a phrase that conveys satiety and completion, matching the following clauses where Paul no longer longs for the Law.
rejected: I am sated with the Law
I am filled with the Law

choices.english: let the mouths of the heretics be put to shame
choices.why: ἐντρέπω in the passive means 'be put to shame'; the verb governs στόματα as subject, so the mouths themselves are shamed, not silenced.
rejected: let the mouths of the heretics be silenced
let the mouths of the heretics be turned away

choices.english: I have become a prisoner of the ray
choices.why: Keeps the metaphor of captivity by light, matching the preceding 'captured by the light' and preserving the noun δεσμώτης as 'prisoner'.
rejected: I have been bound by the ray
I am a captive of the beam

choices.english: does not busy himself with many questions
choices.why: πολυπραγμονέω means to meddle or busy oneself with many things; here it contrasts Paul's simple faith with heretical questioning, so the fuller phrase captures the force.
ἀπαθής is a technical theological term meaning 'not subject to suffering'; 'impassible' is the standard English equivalent and fits the homily's doctrinal point.
κεραμεύω means to work as a potter, to fashion from clay; 'fashioned' preserves the artisan sense without the modern 'ceramic' connotation.

pass_b_english: Why do you make war on me with my own gifts? You fight in defense of the Law, yet you campaign against me; you run for my sake, yet you punish my own people. You avenge my glory, but you do not know where the battle should be joined or where the war should be waged.”

These things Christ says to Saul, and Saul answers and says, “Who are you, Lord?” (Acts 9:5). Paul’s zeal is good, because when he was called he obeyed at once. He received the word and immediately perceived the dignity of the one speaking, and he said, “Who are you, Lord? For I have been filled with the radiance, I have been captured by the light, I have become a prisoner of the ray. “Who are you, Lord?” I long to see your beauty; I am eager to fly up to the clouds; I desire to learn whence comes this “radiance of glory” (Hebrews 1:3), who is the “exact imprint of God’s being” (Hebrews 1:3), who is this one “sustaining all things by the word of his own power” (Hebrews 1:3). “Who are you, Lord?” I have heard your voice, and I have had my fill of the Law; no longer do I long for the Law, no longer do I wish for an ark of gilded wood; I long for a pure manger, wholly royal and honored with gifts of gold.” Let the children of all the heretics be put to shame, and let the mouths of the heretics be put to shame. For see, when Paul was called he does not busy himself with many questions, but only believes; he worships and does not fight; he sings hymns, and faultfinding has been removed. “Who are you, Lord?” he says. He would not have called him Lord if he had not perceived that the one calling him was God. The one he knew as God he confessed as maker; the one he confessed as maker he proclaimed as impassible; he held him as incorruptible. He worshiped as immortal the one whose cross he knew and whose tomb he recognized. He was not ignorant of the blows, the spear in the side, the slaps.

But what does Christ say to him in reply? “I am Jesus the Nazarene, whom you persecute” (Acts 22:8). He receives a concise answer to his question: “I am Jesus the Nazarene, whom you persecute.” I am Jesus, the one who was and who is now, the one before all things and after all things, the one in the beginning and at the last times, the son of David yet himself before David, the maker from Abraham, the one from Adam yet himself the one who fashioned Adam, from Isaac yet himself the one who crowned Isaac’s altar, from Jacob yet himself the one Jacob saw on the ladder, surrounded by the hosts of angels. “I am Jesus, whom you persecute,” but in persecuting you do not overtake me; for where or how will you hunt “the radiance of glory” (Hebrews 1:3)?

problems.why: χρυσόδωρον means 'gifted with gold' (the Magi's gift to the manger), not 'gilded with gold,' which muddles the contrast with the gilded wooden ark.
problems.ruling: χρυσόδωρον is gold-gifted (δῶρον), not covered with gold; 'gilded' blurs contrast with χρυσόξυλον ark.

problems.quote: “I am Jesus the Nazarene, whom you persecute” (Acts 9:5)
problems.source_quote: «Ἐγώ εἰμι Ἰησοῦς ὁ Ναζωραῖος ὃν σὺ διώκεις.»
problems.why: Acts 9:5 omits 'the Nazarene'; the exact quotation with 'the Nazarene' is Acts 22:8.
problems.fix: “I am Jesus the Nazarene, whom you persecute” (Acts 22:8)
problems.ruling: Source has ὁ Ναζωραῖος; tagging Acts 9:5 misleads if that verse lacks Nazarene (Acts 22:8).

problems.quote: and he said, “Who are you, Lord?” For I have been filled with the radiance
problems.source_quote: καὶ ἔλεγεν· «Τίς εἶ, κύριε;» τῇ γὰρ αὐγῇ πεπλήρωμαι
problems.why: Closing the quote after 'Lord?' makes Saul's extended first-person speech (through 'gilded with gold.') read as the author's voice and hides where Hesychius resumes.
problems.fix: and he said, “Who are you, Lord? For I have been filled with the radiance... [closing the quote after 'gold.']
problems.ruling: After ἔλεγεν «Τίς εἶ, κύριε;» τῇ γὰρ αὐγῇ πεπλήρωμαι continues Paul’s first person, not the author.
